patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Dialpad and Vonage share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose Dialpad only if your buying job matches “AI-first cloud phone (Dialpad Connect) with included transcription/summaries — Standard fr” rather than Vonage's shape. Choose Vonage only if your buying job matches “SMB/mid VoIP business phone (VBC) — Mobile from $13.99/line/mo on 12-month promo; Premium/” rather than Dialpad's shape. Workflow advantage differs because Dialpad is shaped for AI-first cloud phone (Dialpad Connect) with included transcription/sum whereas Vonage is shaped for SMB/mid VoIP business phone (VBC) — Mobile from $13.99/line/mo on 12-m. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Dialpad and Vonage share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Dialpad is AI-first cloud phone (Dialpad Connect) with included transcription/summaries — Standard from $15/user/month annual; Sell and Support are sep; Vonage is SMB/mid VoIP business phone (VBC) — Mobile from $13.99/line/mo on 12-month promo; Premium/Advanced higher..
- Company-size focus: Dialpad (small-business, mid-market, enterprise) vs Vonage (solo, small-business, mid-market).
- Researched limits: Dialpad — Pricing page is product-tab heavy — Connect vs Support vs Sell can confuse buyers comparing a single seat price; Vonage — Taxes and regulatory fees sit on top of published per-line floors.

Limitations — Dialpad: Pricing page is product-tab heavy — Connect vs Support vs Sell can confuse buyers comparing a single seat price; Connect Pro has a 3-user minimum; Enterprise requires 100 users; Vonage: Taxes and regulatory fees sit on top of published per-line floors; Call recording and deeper CRM land on Advanced / Premium packaging.

Poor-fit cases: Dialpad is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Pricing page is product-tab heavy — Connect vs Support vs Sell can confuse buyers comparing a single seat price · Vonage is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Taxes and regulatory fees sit on top of published per-line floors · Avoid Dialpad if you actually need Vonage's motion (SMB/mid VoIP business phone (VBC) — Mobile from $13.99/line/mo on 12-month promo)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
